s1.quote: Pamir - this wreck, located to the north of the island is 165ft long and 60 ft deep and offers a relaxing dive - perfect for beginners!

s2.quote: the Pamir remains intact at 40 to 50 ft depth. Host to a colony of black coral and sea fans, you can find schools of sergeant majors, white frogfish, squid, and large pelagic fish.

s3.quote: Pamir Shipwreck - This 165-foot wreck has holes to explore the interior and sits in just 30 to 60 feet (9-18m) of water making it great for all levels of diver.

highlights.text: Black coral, sea fans, frogfish and squid

summary.text: A 165-170 ft freighter sunk as an artificial reef in 1985 off Barbados's west coast, resting upright in roughly 40-60 ft. Easy for all levels, with openings to peek inside and plenty of sponges, sea fans and fish.

s1.quote: Brightledge is a popular reef for the endangered Hawksbill turtle. Excellent visibility and schools of tropicals make this one of the most popular dive sites in Barbados.(int.-adv.)

s2.quote: Bright Ledge - This popular dive site ranges from 65 to over 125 feet (20 to >38m) deep and features colourful corals and sponges along with schools of tropical fish and turtles

highlights.text: Hawksbill turtles, colourful sponges, excellent visibility

summary.text: A popular Barbados west-coast reef ranging from about 65 ft to beyond 125 ft, rated intermediate to advanced. Known for visibility, colourful corals and sponges and hawksbill turtles.

s1.quote: Cement Plant - Great for beginner divers, this shallow site bottoms out around 30 feet (9m) deep. Along with plenty of fish, you may also spot seahorses and lobster! Good night dive location.

s2.quote: The pier of our cement factory at first may seem an unusual dive site, but lobsters, sea horses, frog fish, flying gurnards, arrow crabs, scorpion fish and more abound

highlights.text: Seahorses, frogfish, lobster under the cement pier

summary.text: A shallow dive around a working cement-factory pier on Barbados's west coast, bottoming out near 30 ft. Seahorses, frogfish and lobsters make it a good macro and night dive for beginners.
